summary: Back substitution: row_mem_ofSize_of_dual_frame for X = r⁻¹(1 − u⁻¹) with the vectors uw, its base case from J_T·X = (r⁻¹(1 − u))ᴴ·J_T and the same lemma for r⁻¹(1 − u).

fun i k ↦ mem_ofSize_mono (row_mem_ofSize_of_dual_frame i (h · · |>.elim
  fun w ⟨e, m, n⟩ ↦ ⟨u *ᵥ w, by grind [unitriGroup_mulVec_dual (unipotentBelow_le_unitriGroup hu)
  .refl], fun k ↦ by simpa using (sub_mem_ofSize (mem_ofSize_mono (m k)) (S.2 hr.2 (n k))),

steps.claim: Fix an entry (i, k) of X = r⁻¹(1 − u⁻¹). Apply row_mem_ofSize_of_dual_frame to X and its row i, with the dual-frame vectors of 1.1 (of size c + 2) and the base case of 1.2, at stage j (1.3); monotonicity gives the size c + 4 + (2c + 8)j.

steps.claim: For a pair index a < j, take w from h and use the vector uw: (uw)(e*_b) = w(e*_b) = δ_{ab} for b ≤ a, because u ∈ 𝒩_{<j} ⊂ Q_j fixes these coordinates; uw = w − r·(r⁻¹(1 − u)w) has entries in B^S_{c+2} (B^S_c minus B^S_1·B^S_c); and X(uw) = r⁻¹(1 − u⁻¹)uw = −r⁻¹(1 − u)w has entries in B^S_c (negation axiom), hence in B^S_{c+2}.

steps.lean:
(fun k e ↦ adjoint_apply_mem_ofSize
  (by simp [*, ← inverse_star_unit, ← U.form_mul_inv_eq]) i k fun n l ↦
  (row_mem_ofSize_of_dual_frame n h (fun m _ ↦ by simp [mem_unipotentBelow.1 hu n m (by grind
  [splitGram_eq_ite_oppositeIndex, oppositeIndex_spec, -Sum])]) j · (by lia)))
steps.claim: Base case: for k with j ≤ floorOf(k) or level(k) ≤ ϱ, X_{ik} ∈ B^S_{(c + (c+3)j) + 4}. Since u is unitary and r* = r, J_T·X = (r⁻¹(1 − u))ᴴ·J_T, so adjoint_apply_mem_ofSize applies with Y = r⁻¹(1 − u); its rows Y_n with J_{nk} ≠ 0 have size c + (c+3)j by row_mem_ofSize_of_dual_frame applied to Y (dual-frame vectors from h, base case: Y_{nm} = 0 for the relevant entries, because u ∈ 𝒩_{<j} is block unitriangular there and n is the index opposite to k).
At stage j every basis index k qualifies (j ≤ floorOf(k) + j), giving X_{ik} ∈ B^S_{(c+(c+3)j+4) + (c+5)j}, and c + (c+3)j + 4 + (c+5)j = c + 4 + (2c+8)j (arithmetic by lia).
